personalProjects.name: Observability Platform
personalProjects.description:
[Problem] Metrics and logs from homelab infrastructure were scattered across per-service consoles, slowing root-cause analysis during incidents.
[Solution] Centralized metrics with Prometheus and integrated Loki/Elasticsearch logs into Grafana dashboards. Reproduced the Splunk-based observability operations experience on a Prometheus+Grafana stack.
[Result] Built a unified observability operations platform that cross-analyzes metrics and logs in a single view.

personalProjects.name: n8n Automation
personalProjects.description:
[Problem] Repetitive tasks (Slack alerts, Cloudflare deploy notifications, GitHub Actions result collection) were scattered across crontab and individual scripts, requiring custom code for every new integration.
[Solution] Adopted n8n as a central orchestrator and integrated Slack, GitHub, Cloudflare, and Grafana via webhooks/APIs. Standardized error handling and retries.
[Result] Built a workflow-based automation platform where new integrations can be deployed via UI.

personalProjects.name: FortiManager API Client (Python)
personalProjects.description:
[Problem] Security operations required manually accessing FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer consoles for firewall policy lookups, route inspection, and log statistics.
[Solution] Developed a Python library wrapping FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer REST APIs to abstract policy lookup, route management, and log statistics behind common methods.
[Result] Firewall policy lookups and changes can now be handled via scripts and are used in security operations automation.

en.headline: From OA to DevSecOps — A 8-year Trajectory Built on One Conviction
paragraphs: Nine years ago, I was the person tracking patch schedules for 50 Linux servers on an Excel sheet inside Korea Aerospace Industries' closed network. Repeating the same operations every week led to a single conviction: the value of security operations is not maintaining zero incidents, but automating the guarantee of zero incidents. I spent the next 11 months consecutively earning RHCSA, LPIC-1, and Linux Master Level 2 to rebuild my Linux foundation.

At Metanet M Platform I first picked up Ansible and Python, cutting NAC policy deployment from 10 hours to 1 hour for a 1,000-user contact center. At Jointree, I applied NSX-T microsegmentation to Kookmin University's next-generation information system, eliminating east-west traffic blind spots — blocking 200 monthly intrusion attempts and reducing DLP false positives by 80%. The tools changed, but the principle didn't: any task that requires hands is a candidate for automation.

At Quantec Investment Management's Financial Security Data Center (FSDC), responding to Financial Supervisory Service audits taught me that security operations ultimately means "can you prove it to an auditor with data?" Tuning DB access-control queries from 75% to 52% CPU and validating a PB platform POC were both expressions of one goal: defensible operations.

Today I am embedded in the Nextrade exchange security track, continuously engaged from build (Gaonnuri) into operations (ITCEN CTS). I designed FortiGate HA with 5-tier network segmentation, passed the FSC pre-licensing review, standardized security appliance configuration with Ansible Role (500 firewall policies automated, 8h→1h), and operate Splunk ES detection rules + n8n + FortiManager API automated response (MTTR 30min→12min, 100K+ orders/day). The 24/7 SOC oversees 150 servers, 300 terminals, and 80 network devices.

Next, I want to integrate AI agents with Edge runtimes. My homelab — Cloudflare Workers, MCP, Grafana, Vault — runs on Terraform-managed IaC where I validate "AI handles the first pass of security operations toil" patterns. I want to spend the next nine years not operating the tools that exist, but answering operational problems with new tools.
en.closing: I'd like to bring this trajectory — built on a single question about the limits of repetitive work — to the next problem your security infrastructure needs to solve.
